The ability to leverage the entirety of these datasets is limited to a restricted number of labs with both the capacity and infrastructure to process the data. Whereas Big Data engines have significantly reduced application performance penalties with respect to data movement, their applied strategies (e.g.

arxiv-2111-03399.title: Bottling the Champagne: Dynamics and Radiation Trapping of Wind-Driven Bubbles around Massive Stars 2021 Bottling the Champagne: Dynamics and Radiation Trapping of Wind-Driven Bubbles around Massive Stars – C
arxiv-2111-03399.creator: Sam Geen, Alex de Koter
arxiv-2111-03399.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Sam Geen, Alex de Koter. In this paper we make predictions for the behaviour of wind bubbles around young massive stars using analytic theory. We do this in order to determine why there is a discrepancy between theoretical models that predict that winds should play a secondary role to photoionisation in the dynamics of H ii regions, and observations of young H ii regions that seem to suggest a driving role for winds.

arxiv-2206-02438.title: Body schema or the body as its own best model
arxiv-2206-02438.creator: Matej Hoffmann
arxiv-2206-02438.description: Abstract Abstract Rodney Brooks (1991) put forth the idea that during an agent’s interaction with its environment, representations of the world often stand in the way. Instead, using the world as its own best model, i.e. interacting with it directly without making models, often leads to better and more natural behavior.

arxiv-2310-16981.title: Reimagining Synthetic Tabular Data Generation through Data-Centric AI: A Comprehensive Benchmark
arxiv-2310-16981.creator: Lasse Hansen Aarhus University lasse.hansen@clin.au.dk, Nabeel Seedat University of Cambridge … ns741@cam.ac.uk … Mihaela van der SchaarUniversity of Cambridge ……. mv472@cam.ac.uk ……. Andrija PetrovicUniversity of Belgrade andrija.petrovic@fon.bg.ac.rs
arxiv-2310-16981.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Lasse Hansen Aarhus University lasse.hansen@clin.au.dk, Nabeel Seedat University of Cambridge … ns741@cam.ac.uk … Mihaela van der SchaarUniversity of Cambridge ……. mv472@cam.ac.uk ……. Andrija PetrovicUniversity of Belgrade andrija.petrovic@fon.bg.ac.rs. Synthetic data serves as an alternative in training machine learning models, particularly when real-world data is limited or inaccessible. However, ensuring that synthetic data mirrors the complex nuances of real-world data is a challenging task.

arxiv-2410-03889.title: Identification of Anomalous Geospatial Trajectories via Persistent Homology
arxiv-2410-03889.creator: Evans-Lee, Kyle, Lamb, Kevin
arxiv-2410-03889.description: Abstract We present a novel method for analyzing geospatial trajectory data using topological data analysis (TDA) to identify a specific class of anomalies, commonly referred to as crop circles, in AIS data. This approach is the first of its kind to be applied to spatiotemporal data.

arxiv-2411-06205.title: Suppression of Spin Transfer to Λ \Lambda Hyperon in Deep-Inelastic Scattering
arxiv-2411-06205.creator: Xiaoyan Zhao, Zuo-tang Liang, Tianbo Liu, Ya-jin Zhou
arxiv-2411-06205.description: Abstract We investigate Λ \Lambda production in semi-inclusive deep-inelastic scattering using a polarized lepton beam and find that the spin transfer is significantly suppressed by target fragmentation. As further demonstrated by a model estimation, experimental data can be well described once the target fragmentation is taken into account, which alleviates the tension with calculations solely based on current fragmentation.

arxiv-2412-01845.title: Statistical and Mathematical Evidence of Rigged Parliamentary Elections in Georgia, 2024
arxiv-2412-01845.creator: Lazare Osmanov, Levan Ghaghanidze, Saba Sigua, Temur Begishvili, Keso Bostoghanashvili
arxiv-2412-01845.description: Abstract The official data provided by ”Central Election Commission” was analyzed, revealing irregularities that raised reasonable suspicion of election manipulation by the winning “Georgian Dream Party.” However, these suspicions alone were insufficient to provide concrete evidence. A computational approach was developed based on the official data to address this.

arxiv-2501-16211.title: UDBE: Unsupervised Diffusion-based Brightness Enhancement in Underwater Images
arxiv-2501-16211.creator: 1 st Tatiana Taís Schein, 2 nd Gustavo Pereira de Almeira, 3 rd Stephanie Loi Brião, 4 th Rodrigo Andrade de Bem, 5 th Felipe Gomes de Oliveira, 6 th Paulo L. J. Drews-Jr
arxiv-2501-16211.description: Abstract Activities in underwater environments are paramount in several scenarios, which drives the continuous development of underwater image enhancement techniques. A major challenge in this domain is the depth at which images are captured, with increasing depth resulting in a darker environment.

arxiv-2503-09583.title: Minimax Optimality of the Probability Flow ODE for Diffusion Models 0 0 footnotetext: Corresponding author: Gen Li.
arxiv-2503-09583.creator: Changxiao Cai, Gen Li
arxiv-2503-09583.description: Abstract Score-based diffusion models have become a foundational paradigm for modern generative modeling, demonstrating exceptional capability in generating samples from complex high-dimensional distributions. Despite the dominant adoption of probability flow ODE-based samplers in practice due to their superior sampling efficiency and precision, rigorous statistical guarantees for these methods have remained elusive in the literature.

arxiv-2505-00667.title: A Practical Framework for Simulating Time-Resolved Spectroscopy Based on a Real-time Dyson Expansion
arxiv-2505-00667.creator: Cian C. Reeves, Michael Kurniawan, Yuanran Zhu, Nikil Jampana, Jacob Brown, Chao Yang, Khaled Z. Ibrahim, Vojtech Vlcek
arxiv-2505-00667.description: Abstract Time-resolved spectroscopy is a powerful tool for probing electron dynamics in molecules and solids, revealing transient phenomena on sub-femtosecond timescales. The interpretation of experimental results is often enhanced by parallel numerical studies, which can provide insight and validation for experimental hypotheses. However, developing a theoretical framework for simulating time-resolved spectra remains a significant challenge.

arxiv-2506-01119.title: MOOSE: Pay Attention to Temporal Dynamics for Video Understanding via Optical Flows
arxiv-2506-01119.creator: Hong Nguyen, Dung Tran, Hieu Hoang, Phong Nguyen, Shrikanth Narayanan
arxiv-2506-01119.description: Abstract Many motion-centric video analysis tasks, such as atomic actions, detecting atypical motor behavior in individuals with autism, or analyzing articulatory motion in real-time MRI of human speech, require efficient and interpretable temporal modeling. Capturing temporal dynamics is a central challenge in video analysis, often requiring significant computational resources and fine-grained annotations that are not widely available.

arxiv-2506-21016.title: Fault-Tolerant Spacecraft Attitude Determination using State Estimation Techniques
arxiv-2506-21016.creator: 1 st Bala Chidambaram, 2 nd Anna Hylbert, 3 rd Miggy Silva
arxiv-2506-21016.description: Abstract The extended and unscented Kalman filter, and the particle filter provide a robust framework for fault-tolerant attitude estimation on spacecraft. This paper explores how each filter performs for a large satellite in a low earth orbit. Additionally, various techniques, built on these filters, for fault detection, isolation and recovery from erroneous sensor measurements, are analyzed.

arxiv-2507-01019.title: MALIBU Benchmark: Multi-Agent LLM Implicit Bias Uncovered
arxiv-2507-01019.creator: Imran Mirza, Cole Huang, Ishwara Vasista, Rohan Patil
arxiv-2507-01019.description: Abstract Multi-agent systems, which consist of multiple AI models interacting within a shared environment, are increasingly used for persona-based interactions. However, if not carefully designed, these systems can reinforce implicit biases in large language models (LLMs), raising concerns about fairness and equitable representation. We present MALIBU 1 1 1 You can find the MALIBU Benchmark here: https://anonymous.4open.

arxiv-2510-09136.creator: Marlene Holzleitner, Stephan Leitner, Hanna Lind Jorgensen, Christoph Schmitz, Jacob Welander, Dietmar Jannach
arxiv-2510-09136.description: Abstract . Personalized news recommendations have become a standard feature of large news aggregation services, optimizing user engagement through automated content selection. In contrast, legacy news media often approach personalization cautiously, striving to balance technological innovation with core editorial values.

plos-pone-0012817.description: PLOS ONE research article. Musladin-Lueke Syndrome (MLS) is a hereditary disorder affecting Beagle dogs that manifests with extensive fibrosis of the skin and joints. In this respect, it resembles human stiff skin syndrome and the Tight skin mouse, each of which is caused by gene defects affecting fibrilli

pmc-10623745.title: Causal association of epigenetic aging and osteoporosis: a bidirectional Mendelian randomization study
pmc-10623745.creator: Xinyu Liang, Wei Shi, Xinglong Zhang, Ran Pang, Kai Zhang, Qian Xu, Chunlei Xu, Xin Wan, Wenhao Cui, Dong Li, Zhaohui Jiang, Zhengxuan Liu, Hui Li, Huafeng Zhang, Zhijun Li
pmc-10623745.description: BackgroundThe relationship between aging and osteoporosis is well established. However, the relationship between the body's physiological age, i.e. epigenetic age, and osteoporosis is not known. Our goal is to analyze the bidirectional causal relationship between epigenetic clocks and osteoporosis using a bidirectional Mendelian randomization study.

pmc-10772775.title: Mutation Analysis of KRAS and BRAF in Iranian Colorectal Cancer patients: A Novel Variant in Exon 15 of BRAF
pmc-10772775.creator: Bita Hassani, Rasoul Alizadeh, Mansoureh Akouchekian, Fahimeh Safarnezhad Tameshkel, Mohammad Hadi Karbalaie Niya
pmc-10772775.description: Background:Mitogen-Activated Protein Kinase (MAPK) pathway and its downstream signaling pathways, play an important role in intracellular signaling. Mutations in KRAS (activating mutation) and BRAF proto-oncogenes are identified as key finding of colorectal cancer. The aim of this study was to examine mutation analysis of KRAS and BRAF in Iranian Colorectal cancer patients.

pmc-11327268.title: Metastatic sinonasal malignancies of colorectal origin: Case report and comprehensive review of the literature
pmc-11327268.creator: Andrew J. Rothka, David Goldrich, Jessyka G. Lighthall
pmc-11327268.description: Key Clinical MessagePrimary adenocarcinomas represent a small percentage of sinonasal malignancies. Metastasis of colorectal malignancies to the paranasal sinuses is rare, poorly understood, and typically fatal. This case documents an unusual source of metastatic sinonasal malignancy and offers comparison to a cohort of similar patients found in the literature.

pmc-11364706.title: Association between antibiotics use and osteoporotic fracture risk: a nationally representative retrospective cohort study
pmc-11364706.creator: Ji Won Lee, Sun Jae Park, Young Jun Park, Seogsong Jeong, Jihun Song, Hye Jun Kim, Jooyoung Chang, Kyae Hyung Kim, Ji Soo Kim, Yun Hwan Oh, Yoosun Cho, Sang Min Park
pmc-11364706.description: SummaryThis population-based retrospective cohort study aimed to estimate the association between antibiotic exposure and osteoporotic fracture risk. Long-term antibiotic use was associated with the risk of osteoporotic fracture. An increase in the number of antibiotic classes prescribed may also be associated with an increased osteoporotic fracture risk.

pmc-11628802.title: Exemplifying interspecies variation of liposome in vivo fate by the effects of anti-PEG antibodies
pmc-11628802.creator: Ercan Wu, Juan Guan, Yifei Yu, Shiqi Lin, Tianhao Ding, Yuxiu Chu, Feng Pan, Mengyuan Liu, Yang Yang, Zui Zhang, Jian Zhang, Changyou Zhan, Jun Qian
pmc-11628802.description: The different fate of liposomes among species has been discovered and mentioned in many studies, but the underlying mechanisms have not been explored. In the present work, we concentrated on the in vivo fate of PEGylated liposomes (sLip) in three commonly used species (mice, rats, and dogs).

pmc-11690610.title: EXPERT BY EXPERIENCE WITH DEMENTIA CO-TEACHING: HAVING AN EXPERT IN EVERY CLASS
pmc-11690610.creator: Michelle Kimzey
pmc-11690610.description: Care for people with dementia requires a better understanding of the reality of dementia. People with dementia are the true experts on dementia because they are living the experience. Including them in the teaching role benefits students and a person with dementia.

pmc-11710529.title: Progranulin acts in lysosomes to promote neuronal survival and growth
pmc-11710529.creator: Azariah K Kaplelach, Justin A Hall, Skylar E Davis, Jonathan R Roth, Qays Aljabi, Ahmad R Hakim, Katherine Savell, Jeremy J Day, Andrew E Arrant
pmc-11710529.description: Progranulin is a secreted pro‐protein that is necessary for maintaining lysosomal function and exerts anti‐inflammatory and neurotrophic effects in the brain. Loss‐of‐function GRN mutations, most of which cause progranulin haploinsufficiency, are a major autosomal dominant cause of frontotemporal dementia (FTD). Other GRN variants are associated with risk for FTD, Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and Parkinson’s disease.

pmc-11715636.title: High‐performance plasma proteomic biomarker candidates in early Alzheimer's disease
pmc-11715636.creator: Yuhan Xie, Hui Sun, Fang Liu, Yaonan Zheng, Mang Zhang, Xin Ma, Xin Yu, nan zhang, chaolan huang, Huali Wang
pmc-11715636.description: BackgroundThe present study aimed to establish a panel of plasma proteins that are associated with cognitive performance and amyloid‐β burden and establish their utility for distinguishing early Alzheimer’s disease (AD) from healthy controls.MethodPlasma from fifty patients with early AD (all amyloid‐positive) and forty‐nine healthy controls (HCs) were assayed using quantitative mass spectrometry.

pmc-12606953.title: Effectiveness of tafenoquine and primaquine for radical cure of Plasmodium vivax: a meeting report from dissemination of results of the EFFORT trial to stakeholders in Pakistan
pmc-12606953.creator: Bushra Qurashi, Shan-e-Zehra Zaidi, Muhammad Mushtaque, Ahmed Faisal, Zeeshan Haroon, Baseer Agha, Naseer Hammal, Abdul Hameed, Ali Raza, Umair Ali, Asia Khan, Fareeha Abdul Jabbar, Zainab Rafeeq Adam, Tariq Mehmood, Ric N Price, Najia Ghanchi, Kamala Thriemer, M Asim Beg
pmc-12606953.description: Plasmodium vivax remains the predominant cause of malaria in Pakistan, accounting for approximately 85% of confirmed cases. The recurrent nature of P. vivax, driven by dormant liver-stage hypnozoites, poses a major obstacle to malaria control. Pakistan currently uses a 14-day low-dose primaquine regimen (3.5 mg/kg total dose) without routine G6PD testing, a strategy limited by poor adherence and suboptimal efficacy.

pmc-13332897.title: Case report: exercise-associated sudden death in a Thoroughbred racehorse with cardiac lesions
pmc-13332897.creator: Hernando Daniel Acevedo, Francisco Uzal, Jeff Blea, Eileen Henderson, Akinyi Nyaoke, Carlos Omar Schild, Javier Asin
pmc-13332897.description: Exercise-associated sudden death (EASD), defined as acute collapse and death in an apparently healthy racehorse during or within ~1 h after exercise, is currently among the top concerns in the racing industry. Cases of EASD with no cause of death identified at necropsy are frequently presumed to be of cardiac origin.

pmc-13473921.title: Psychosocial Adaptation, Disability, and Resilience among Individuals with Amputations in an Indian setting
pmc-13473921.creator: Lishma Shann Mathew, Anandha Ruby Jacob, Sheeba Rani. P, Grace Rebekah, Judy Ann John
pmc-13473921.description: Background:Traumatic amputations significantly affect physical function, coping, and self-esteem, highlighting the need for comprehensive rehabilitation and holistic nursing care. The study aims to assess the functional disability, coping strategies, and self-esteem of patients with upper or lower limb amputation.Methodology:Overall, 250 subjects were recruited from various departments and their services for this cross-sectional correlational study.

pmc-13525161.title: The new (version 9) American Joint Committee on Cancer (AJCC) tumor‐node‐metastasis (TNM) staging protocol for carcinoma of the vulva
pmc-13525161.creator: Alexander B. Olawaiye, Elliot A. Asare, Ian S. Hagemann, Priya R. Bhosale, Stephanie Gaillard, Brian Rous, Bunja Rungruang, Shitanshu Uppal, Gulisa Turashvili, Kaled M. Alektiar, Jonathan A. Cosin, Uma Krishnamurti, Lee‐may Chen, Keiichi Fujiwara, Matthew A. Powell, Mauricio A. Cuello, David G. Mutc
pmc-13525161.description: The American Joint Committee on Cancer (AJCC) tumor‐node‐metastasis (TNM) staging for all cancer sites has been updated periodically as a published manual for many years. The last update of the manual version, the eighth edition AJCC Cancer Staging Manual, went into use on January 1, 2018.

pmc-13629238.title: Repeated evolution of convergent iridescence in closely related species of Morpho butterflies living in sympatry
pmc-13629238.creator: Joséphine Ledamoisel, Vincent Debat, Violaine Llaurens
pmc-13629238.description: The evolution of visual traits in closely related species living in sympatry is highly influenced by their ecological interactions: while sexual selection tends to promote the divergence of visual cues involved in mate choice, natural selection via predation may promote the convergence of dissuasive signals between prey species, especially in unpalatable or evasive prey.
